subject: profit-break-even
title: Break-Even, Operating Leverage, and Margin of Safety
summary: The CVP toolkit applied to a startup decision, with the traps.

cards.title: Same revenue, different risk
cards.text: Two businesses each sell $100k a year. One has mostly fixed costs, the other mostly variable. Revenue drops 20%. Which one is in trouble, and how fast?

cards.title: The SBA formulas
cards.text: Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost per unit). Break-even dollars = fixed costs ÷ contribution margin ratio, where the ratio = (price − variable cost) ÷ price. The SBA builds its calculator on monthly figures.
cards.example: Example: $40k of fixed costs and a 40% contribution margin ratio give $100k of break-even revenue.

cards.title: Operating leverage
cards.text: Business A: $60k fixed, 70% contribution margin ratio. Business B: $10k fixed, 20% ratio. At $100k revenue both earn $10k. At $80k, A earns −$4k and B earns $6k. At $120k, A earns $24k and B earns $14k. High fixed costs amplify both directions.

cards.title: Margin of safety
cards.text: Margin of safety = (current revenue − break-even revenue) ÷ current revenue. A has break-even revenue of about $85.7k, so a 14% margin at $100k. B breaks even at $50k, a 50% margin. The SBA also suggests padding costs by about 10% for unpredictable expenses.

cards.title: Where it misleads
cards.text: CVP assumes linear prices and costs and a single product (or a stable mix). The SBA itself calls break-even an estimate for planning and lenders, not precise accounting. Step-fixed costs, volume discounts, and mix shifts break the straight lines.

cards.question: For a business you know well, is the cost structure a deliberate choice or an accident? What would it take to move fixed costs to variable, or the reverse, and when would you want to?
nudges: Think of outsourcing, leasing vs. buying, and revenue-share deals.
How volatile is demand, and how confident are you in it?

questions.q: Fixed costs $40k, contribution margin ratio 40%. Break-even revenue?

Which is a core limitation of break-even analysis?

options.text: It assumes linear costs and prices and a stable product mix.
options.why: Right. Real cost curves have steps and discounts.
Fixed costs are central to it.

options.text: It can't be computed in dollars.
options.why: The SBA gives a dollar formula.
The SBA says it is usually required by investors and lenders.

cards.prompt: Explain this to someone at dinner in 3 sentences.

sources.title: Break-even point
sources.supports: Break-even is where total cost equals total revenue; fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost) = break-even units; contribution margin; fixed vs. variable costs; adding about 10% for unexpected expenses; why investors and lenders ask for it.
